title: Starting and finishing
about: Collocations for beginnings and endings: make a promising or early start, get off to a good start, a close or nail-biting finish, put the finishing touches to something, and things that come to an end, draw to a close or end abruptly.

parts.title: More collocations for starting and finishing
Common mistakes
parts.note: Про відпустку, подорож, поїздку чи обід (вечерю) природніше казати ended, а не finished: Our holiday ended with a day in Rome. Finish — коли людина доводить до кінця свою справу (finish work, finish your soup, finish a book), і фініш у змаганні (a close finish); про те, що закінчується за розкладом, кажуть і finish: The film finishes at ten. У таблиці — пастки цього юніту.

items.pattern: make a promising / good / bright start (in / on sth) · opposite: make a poor / disappointing start
items.meaning: begin something well, so that people expect it to go well later
items.example: The new bakery on our street has **made a promising start**: there's a queue outside every morning.
more: My nephew has **made a promising start** at university and loves his course.
We **made a promising start** on our healthy-eating plan, but by Friday we were eating chips again.
items.watchOut: «Перспективний, багатообіцяючий» — promising, а не perspective: perspective — це «погляд, точка зору». Зі start дієслово make, а не do: make a promising start.

items.pattern: make an early / a late start (to / on sth) · have (got) an early start = need to get up early
items.meaning: begin a journey or a day's work early in the morning
items.example: If we **make an early start**, we'll miss the traffic on the way to the coast.
more: Mum has **an early start** on Mondays: her shift at the hospital begins at six.
We **made a late start** because of the snow, so we reached the hotel after midnight.
items.watchOut: «Рано вирушити» — make an early start, а не do an early start. I've got an early start tomorrow — «мені завтра рано вставати». Протилежне — make a late start.

items.pattern: traffic builds up / is building up (on a road) · a build-up of traffic · heavy traffic
items.meaning: more and more cars come onto the road, so it gets slow and crowded
items.example: By half past seven, **traffic** was already **building up** on the ring road.
more: Leave before four, because **traffic builds up** quickly near the shopping centre.
There was a long **build-up of traffic** after the accident on the bridge.
items.watchOut: Traffic — незлічуване: traffic is building up, а не traffics are. «Сильний рух» — heavy traffic, а не big traffic. «Рух» на дорозі — traffic, а не movement.

items.pattern: an absolute / a complete / a total beginner (at / in sth) · a class for absolute beginners · an absolute beginners' course
items.meaning: someone who is just starting to learn something and knows nothing about it yet
items.uk: абсолютний (повний) новачок, той, хто починає з нуля
items.example: I'm an **absolute beginner** at golf: I've never even held a club.
more: The dance school runs a class for **absolute beginners** on Tuesday evenings.
Grandma taught me to knit when I was an **absolute beginner**, and now I make all my own scarves.
items.watchOut: «Повний новачок, з нуля» — an absolute (complete, total) beginner, а не a zero beginner чи a full beginner. Наголос на першому складі: ABsolute.

items.phrase: get off to a good start
items.pattern: get off to a good / great / flying start · opposite: get off to a bad / slow / shaky start
items.meaning: begin well (or badly): an event, a trip, a season, a day
items.example: The school fair **got off to a good start**: the cakes sold out in an hour.
more: My day **got off to a bad start** when I missed the bus in the rain.
Our holiday **got off to a flying start**: the plane landed twenty minutes early.
items.watchOut: Off тут обов'язкове: get off to a good start, а не get to a good start чи go off to a good start. «Взяти хороший старт» дослівно не перекладай. A flying start — блискучий, дуже швидкий початок.

items.pattern: a (very) close finish (to a race / match / vote) · finish = the last part of a race
items.meaning: the end of a race or competition when the winner is only just ahead
items.uk: щільний фініш, перемога з мінімальним відривом
items.example: The village bake-off had **a close finish**: Mrs Hall beat my mum by a single point.
more: After **a close finish**, the two swimmers hugged in the water.
Our street's charity run had **a close finish**: my neighbour beat me by a metre.
items.watchOut: «Щільний фініш» — a close finish, а не a near finish: near — про відстань (near the station). Finish як іменник — фініш у змаганні; кінець фільму чи відпустки — end.

items.pattern: a nail-biting finish / match / final / wait
items.meaning: an end to a race or game that is so exciting and tense that you can hardly watch
items.uk: фініш, від якого завмирає серце; дуже напружена розв'язка
items.example: The tennis final had **a nail-biting finish**, and Grandad couldn't sit down for the last ten minutes.
more: Our quiz team won in **a nail-biting finish**, on the very last question.
We watched the boat race on TV, and it had **a nail-biting finish**.
items.watchOut: «Нервовий фініш» — зазвичай a nail-biting (або nerve-racking) finish, а не a nervous finish: nervous частіше описує людину, яка нервує. Nail-biting дослівно — «такий, що аж гризеш нігті».

items.phrase: put the finishing touches to sth
items.pattern: put / add the finishing touches to sth (AmE also on sth) · similar: the final touches
items.meaning: do the last small things that make a piece of work complete or perfect
items.example: Mum is **putting the finishing touches to** the birthday cake: only the candles and sprinkles are left.
more: We **put the finishing touches to** the spare room before Grandma arrived: fresh flowers and a new lamp.
Give me five minutes. I'm just **adding the finishing touches to** my make-up.
items.watchOut: «Останні штрихи» — the finishing (або final) touches, а не the last strokes чи the ending touches. Дієслово put або add, прийменник to: put the finishing touches to the room.

items.pattern: bring sth to an end · sth is brought to an end · bring sth to an abrupt / sudden end · similar: put an end to sth
items.meaning: make something finish, often something that has gone on for a long time
items.example: A long talk over dinner finally **brought** the argument between the two sisters **to an end**.
more: The rain **brought** our picnic **to an end** after only twenty minutes.
The new fence **brought** years of arguing with the neighbours about their dog **to an end**.
items.watchOut: «Покласти край» — bring sth to an end, а не take sth to an end чи lead sth to an end. Близький варіант — put an end to sth; зверни увагу на порядок слів: put an end to the noise, але bring the noise to an end. З прикметником можна й так: bring an abrupt end to sth.

items.phrase: mark the beginning of the end
items.pattern: mark / be / signal the beginning of the end (for / of sb/sth)
items.meaning: be the first sign that something will soon finish or fail
items.example: When the big supermarket opened, it **marked the beginning of the end** for the little shops on our street.
more: The first cold night **marked the beginning of the end** for the tomatoes in our garden.
That first argument about money **was the beginning of the end** of their friendship.
items.watchOut: «Початок кінця» — сталий вираз the beginning of the end, а не the start of the end. Дієслово часто mark — «знаменувати, позначати».

items.pattern: the end result (of sth) · The end result was that… · similar: the final result
items.meaning: what you finally get after a long process or a lot of effort
items.example: We sanded and painted the old chair three times, and the **end result** looks brand new.
more: Months of saving, and the **end result** was a week in Greece for the whole family.
I followed the recipe exactly, but the **end result** looked nothing like the photo.
items.watchOut: «Кінцевий результат» — the end result або the final result, а не the finish result чи the ending result. End тут стоїть перед іменником як означення.

items.pattern: a / the perfect end to sth (a day / holiday / evening) · also: a lovely / fitting end to sth
items.meaning: the best possible way for something good to finish
items.example: Fish and chips on the beach was **a perfect end to** our day at the seaside.
more: A hot bath and an early night are **the perfect end to** a long week.
The fireworks over the lake were **a perfect end to** the wedding.
items.watchOut: Після end тут зазвичай to: a perfect end to the holiday (of трапляється рідше). Про саму відпустку чи поїздку природніше казати ended, а не finished: Our holiday ended on a rainy Sunday.

items.pattern: make a start (on sth) · get started (on / with sth) · Let's make a start / get started
items.meaning: begin doing something, especially a piece of work
items.example: Let's **make a start** on the garden early, before it gets too hot.
more: Everyone's here, so shall we **get started**?
I need to **get started on** my packing: our flight's at six tomorrow.
items.watchOut: «Почнімо» — Let's make a start або Let's get started, а не Let's do a start. Після get started іде прийменник: get started on the cleaning, а не get started the cleaning.

items.pattern: sth comes to an end · come to an abrupt / sudden end · compare: come to the end of sth (reach its last part)
items.meaning: finish; stop happening (an event, a period of time, a relationship)
items.example: When the summer holidays **came to an end**, the kids were secretly glad to see their friends again.
more: Even the longest queue **comes to an end** eventually.
Their marriage **came to an end** after twelve years, but they're still good friends.
items.watchOut: «Добігти кінця» — come to an end, а не go to an end. Не плутай з come to the end of sth — «дійти до кінця чогось»: We came to the end of the road.

items.pattern: sth draws / is drawing to a close · similar: come to a close · formal: draw sth to a close
items.meaning: slowly come to the end (an evening, a meeting, a year); a little formal
items.example: As the evening **drew to a close**, our hosts brought out coffee and chocolates.
more: The school year is **drawing to a close**, and the children can't stop talking about summer.
The festival **drew to a close** with a concert in the main square.
items.watchOut: Дієслово draw, а не pull чи go: The day is drawing to a close. Draw to a close звучить трохи книжніше, ніж come to an end, і часто стоїть у Continuous: поступово добігає кінця.

items.pattern: an abrupt end (to sth) · come to an abrupt end · bring / put an abrupt end to sth · similar: a sudden end
items.meaning: a sudden and unexpected end, usually an unwelcome one
items.example: Our barbecue came to **an abrupt end** when a thunderstorm started.
more: A broken leg put **an abrupt end** to his football season.
The power cut brought **an abrupt end** to the school disco.
items.watchOut: «Різко обірватися» — come to an abrupt (або a sudden) end. A sharp end у цьому значенні не кажуть: the sharp end — найважча, найнебезпечніша ділянка справи. Наголос на другому складі: abRUPT.

warmup.uk: Гості прийдуть о сьомій, тож давай уже братися до готування.
warmup.q: The guests are coming at seven, so let's ___ a start on the cooking.
warmup.explain: Почати, взятися до справи — make a start (on sth) або get started. Do a start не кажуть.

warmup.uk: Ми додаємо останні штрихи до святкового столу.
warmup.q: We're putting the ___ to the party table.
warmup.explain: Останні штрихи — the finishing (або final) touches; strokes тут не кажуть.

warmup.q: The ___ result surprised all of us.
warmup.explain: Кінцевий результат — the end result (або the final result).

warmup.q: Our new coach has made a ___ start.
warmup.explain: Перспективний, багатообіцяючий — promising. Perspective — погляд, точка зору; prospective — майбутній, можливий.

warmup.uk: Вечірка добігла кінця о другій ночі.
warmup.q: The party ___ to an end at two in the morning.
warmup.explain: Закінчитися, добігти кінця — come to an end.
Повний новачок — an absolute (complete, total) beginner.

warmup.uk: Дзвінок від начальника поклав край моїй відпустці.
warmup.q: A call from my boss ___ my holiday to an end.
warmup.explain: Покласти край чомусь — bring sth to an end (або put an end to sth).

warmup.uk: Сезон у нашої футбольної команди почався чудово: три перемоги поспіль.
warmup.q: Our football team's season got ___ to a great start: three wins in a row.
warmup.explain: Добре почати(ся) — get off to a good / great start. Off тут обов'язкове.

A.q: Our new neighbour has made a ___ start in the village choir: they've already given her a solo.
A.explain: Багатообіцяючий початок — a promising start. Perspective — погляд, точка зору; promised — обіцяний.

A.q: We always do our weekly shop early on Saturday, before the traffic starts ___ up in town.
A.explain: Traffic builds up — рух щільнішає, збираються затори.

A.q: On my first day at the climbing wall I was ___ beginner, so the instructor stayed close.
A.explain: Повний новачок — an absolute (complete, total) beginner. Full і whole з beginner не вживають.

B.q: The vote for head of the parents' committee had a very ___ finish: Anna won by two votes.
B.explain: Перемога з мінімальним відривом — a close finish. Near — про відстань.

B.q: The builders are just putting the ___ touches to our new kitchen.
B.explain: Останні штрихи — the finishing (або final) touches.

B.q: A burst pipe in the bathroom ___ our dinner party to an end.
B.explain: Покласти край — bring sth to an end, а не take чи lead.

C.q: Our week at the lake ___ to a close, and we packed the car in silence.
C.explain: Добігати кінця — draw to a close.

C.q: The street party, with music and dancing until late, was a perfect end ___ the school year.
C.explain: A perfect end to sth — після end прийменник to.

C.q: A wasp in the car brought ___ end to our sing-along on the way to the beach.
C.explain: Раптовий кінець — an abrupt (або a sudden) end. Sharp і steep тут не підходять.

example.title: Sports day
example.uk:
Спортивне свято в школі мого сина почалося невдало. Ми вирушили рано, але біля школи вже збиралися затори, і ми пропустили перший забіг.

У забігу для батьків я почувався абсолютним новачком: я не бігав двадцять років. Фініш був щільний: я прийшов другим, на кілька сантиметрів позаду переможця. Потім команда мого сина виграла естафету у фінішній боротьбі, від якої завмирало серце.

Поки вчителі додавали останні штрихи до столу з призами, ми влаштували пікнік на траві. Коли свято добігало кінця, почався дощ. Кінцевий результат? Одна медаль, двоє мокрих дітей і болюча нога. Та все ж морозиво дорогою додому стало ідеальним завершенням дня.
example.en:
Sports day at my son's school [[got off to a bad start|a5]]. We [[made an early start|a2]], but [[traffic was already building up|a3]] near the school, and we missed the first race.

In the parents' race, I felt like an [[absolute beginner|a4]]: I hadn't run for twenty years. It was a [[close finish|b1]]: I came second, a few centimetres behind the winner. Then my son's team won the relay in a [[nail-biting finish|b2]].

While the teachers [[put the finishing touches to|b3]] the prize table, we had a picnic on the grass. As sports day [[drew to a close|c6]], it started to rain. The [[end result|c2]]? One medal, two wet children and a sore leg. Still, an ice cream on the way home was a [[perfect end to|c3]] the day.
